ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the altitude from $A$ to side $BC$, and $BE$ is an angle bisector, intersecting at point $P$. Given that $\angle EPD=120^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle BAD=x^\circ$\\
Given the problem, we have: $\angle BDA=90^\circ$, $\angle ABE=\angle CBE=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABD=90^\circ-x^\circ$, $\angle ABE=\angle CBE=45^\circ-\frac{x^\circ}{2}$,\\
By the exterior angle property of triangles, we get $\angle EBD+\angle BDA=\angle DPE$,\\
that is $45^\circ-\frac{x^\circ}{2}+90^\circ=120^\circ$, solving this gives $x=\boxed{30}$,\\
hence $\angle BAD=\boxed{30^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the base BC of triangle ABC is horizontal, and A is above; D is on BC, and AD drops vertically from A to the base, indicating that AD is the altitude to BC, therefore AD ⟂ BC. Point E is on side AC, and segment BE is drawn from B to E and intersects AD at P; therefore B, P, E are collinear, and D, P, A are collinear. Reasoning: Let ∠BAD = x°. Because AD ⟂ BC and D is on BC, ∠BDA = 90°. In right triangle ABD, ∠ABD = 90° - x°. Also because BE is the angle bisector of ∠ABC, and BD and BC are on the same straight line, ∠EBD is half of ∠ABD, that is, ∠EBD = (90° - x°)/2 = 45° - x°/2. In triangle BDP, PE is the extension of PB, so ∠EPD is the exterior angle of triangle BDP at P, equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles: ∠EPD = ∠EBD + ∠BDP. Here ∠BDP = 90°, and it is known that ∠EPD = 120°, so (45° - x°/2) + 90° = 120°. Solving gives 135° - x°/2 = 120°, so x°/2 = 15°, x = 30. Therefore ∠BAD = 30°.
